s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Skin lesions are present on periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles

Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism

Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis

differentials: talaromyces marneffei infection with ifngr1 gene mutation

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Dense granulomatous infiltrate and presence of multinucleated giant cells in skin biopsy

shortlist.label: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with granulomatous infiltrate and presence of histiocytes, lymphocytes, and multinucleated giant cells

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with granulomatous infiltrate, although immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100

shortlist.label: Indeterminate dendritic cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with dense granulomatous infiltrate and presence of histiocytes, lymphocytes, and multinucleated giant cells

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with granulomatous infiltrate, and presence of central diabetes insipidus and other systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's 7-year medical history of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques, along with the presence of central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, are consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease. The skin biopsy findings of a dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis with negative CD1a and S-100 and positive CD68 immunohistochemical results also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with fewer lesions and lacks the systemic involvement seen in this patient

rejected.label: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis
rejected.why: Characterized by mucocutaneous lesions and often associated with arthritis, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically has positive CD1a and S-100 immunohistochemical results, which is not consistent with this patient's biopsy findings

rejected.label: Indeterminate dendritic cell tumor
rejected.why: Rare and lacks the distinct clinical and histological features seen in this patient
